Chapter 7: Navigating Resistance and Emotional Turbulence
As you start planting new beliefs and habits, you might notice something popping up—resistance. It’s totally normal, and honestly, it happens to everyone. Our minds love to stick with what’s familiar, like walking the same old path through the woods. But when you step off that path and try something new, you might feel a wave of discomfort, a little doubt, or even fear.
Resistance can sneak in as procrastination, self-sabotage, or a rush of anxiety that seems to come out of nowhere. Sometimes, it’s the world around you that pushes back—a friend questions your decision, or an unexpected obstacle shows up just as you’re gaining momentum.
But here’s something to pay attention to: resistance doesn’t mean you’re failing. In fact, it’s often a sign that real change is starting to happen. Your system is adjusting, and those old patterns are just putting up a final fight.
So, how do you navigate this emotional turbulence? Let’s talk about a few strategies that can really help:
First, try naming the resistance. When you feel that discomfort or anxiety, acknowledge it. You might say to yourself, “I notice I’m feeling nervous about this new step.” Just naming the feeling can create a bit of distance, and suddenly, it doesn’t hold as much power over you.
Next, stay with the feeling. Instead of distracting yourself or trying to push it away, let it be there. Notice where it shows up in your body. Maybe it’s a tightness in your chest or butterflies in your stomach. Breathe into it. More often than not, the intensity fades on its own.
And don’t forget to revisit your “why.” Remind yourself why you’re making these changes in the first place. What do you want to experience or create in your life? Reconnecting with your deeper motivation gives you the energy to move through resistance.
Picture someone who’s learning to set boundaries for the first time. That first “no” can bring up guilt or fear of being rejected. But by staying present with those feelings and remembering their desire for healthier relationships, they find the strength to hold that boundary—even when it feels uncomfortable.
So, here’s the key takeaway: resistance isn’t a sign to turn back. It’s a natural part of growing and changing. Each time you move through it, you’re building resilience and making your new way of being that much stronger.
